newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-RINKER TAKES FIRST-ROUND LEAD IN CALIFORNIA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RINKER TAKES FIRST-ROUND LEAD IN CALIFORNIA.

text.p: Larry Rinker, who lost his Tour card three years ago, used a sponsor's exemption to take the lead after the first round at the Bob Hope Classic golf tournament with a 63 on Wednesday.
Rinker's nine under par gave him a one-stroke advantage over U.S. Open champion Steve Jones, and Mark Calcavecchia.
John Daly was among a group of four two strokes off the pace with 65s.
The Bob Hope Classic is a five day, 90-hole event, with the first four rounds played in a pro-am format over four desert courses.

Rinker shot his 63 at Bermuda Dunes. Jones played Indian Ridge, and Calcavecchia was on the Indian Wells host course. The other course, La Quinta, is consider the most difficult of the four and yielded far fewer sub-par scores than the others.

Rinker said he was anxious at the start of the round, and missed an eight-foot birdie putt on his first hole. But then he birdied the next five in a row. Rinker had five more birdies, including three in succession to close his round. He also had a bogey.
"This week I think you've got to have the attitude that you need to get to about 25 under," Rinker said. "It's a long week."
Jones' 64 was his best round since winning the U.S. Open.
"Since Tiger's not in the field, we all have a chance," said Jones, referring to rookie sensation Tiger Woods.
Jones was bogeyless on Wednesday, making eight birdies, all but two from putts inside of six feet.
Calcavecchia was tied for the lead until he three-putted the last green, lipping out a four footer for par. He also had seven birdies and an eagle.
